Contact.description: Describes an individual Contact listing record. At least one of the following are required to identify the customer: `email`, `customer_id`, `phone_number`, or `extra_identifiers` (any one entry satisfies the requirement). Ometria attempts to merge each contact record into a single profile using the identifiers configured for your account; by default these are `customer_id` and then `email`. Accounts using identity resolution can configure additional identifiers and control how they are matched and merged.

@add_to_lists.description: The ID of the segment you want to send this contact to, max length: 16.

@collection.description: The collection you want the contact to belong to.

@force_optin.description: If 'True', this field overrides marketing opt-in priority.

@merge.description: If 'True', this call will not override blank fields (i.e. fields that exist but aren't passed)

@remove_from_lists.description: The ID of the segment you want to remove this contact from, max length: 16.

@type.description: The value must be "contact". This shows that this record represents a contact object.

channels.description: Contact preferences across different communication channels, e.g. SMS

allow_marketing.description: Whether the contact is opted in/out for SMS marketing. If left out, this implies unspecified.

allow_transactional.description: Whether the contact is opted in/out to transactional SMS. If left out, it implies 'unspecified'.

dt_updated_marketing.description:
The date and time the contact updated their marketing SMS preference.
Onlyprovide if known.
Follow ISO 8601 DateTime format with timezone offset YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+Z

dt_updated_transactional.description:
The date and time the contact updated their transactional SMS preference. Only
provide if known.
Follow ISO 8601 DateTime format with timezone offset YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+Z

country_id.description:
The contact's country, must be 2 characters, upper case, e.g. 'GB'.
Follow ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.
If you exceed the character limit this field will pass validation but appear truncated in Ometria.
If left empty this field will be set to 'null'.

customer_id.description:
Your universal customer ID for this contact, if applicable. max length: 255.
Only use this value if the customer ID is persistent across all your systems (that send data to Ometria).
You must include either `email` or `customer_id` in every record. Some retailers can also use the `phone_number` or `extra_identifiers` field - speak to your Customer Success Representative if you're unsure.

date_of_birth.description:
The contact's date of birth.
Following ISO 8601 date format YYYY-MM-DD.

email.description:
The contact's email address, max length: 255, lower case.
If left empty this field will be set to 'null'.
You must include either `email` or `customer_id` in every record. Some retailers can also use the `phone_number` or `extra_identifiers` field - speak to your Customer Success Representative if you're unsure.

extra_identifiers.description: Optional list of extra identifiers (such as a loyalty ID) as per your identity resolution configuration, e.g. `loyalty_id`. Custom identifiers must be configured for your account before you send them. See Custom identifiers for the full format, multi-valued identifiers, and CSV usage.

firstname.description: The contact's first name, max length: 64.

gender.description:
The contact's gender.
We currently support the values "m" (man), "f" (woman) and "o" (other).
Use the value "o" when the contact's gender is known but it is not "m" or "f". If the contact's gender is unknown then the field "gender" should not be included.
If left empty, gender is inferred from the contact's prefix (e.g 'Ms' will be 'f').

id.description: The ID of this listing within the collection, max length: 255

lastname.description: The contact's last name, max length: 64.

middlename.description: The contact's middle name, max length: 64.

phone_number.description:
The contact's mobile phone number, in E.164/International format (e.g. starting "+447...") or National format (without the country code prefix, please note that country_id is required in order to validate the phone number in this format).
You must include either `email` or `customer_id` in every record. Some retailers can also use the `phone_number` or `extra_identifiers` field - speak to your Customer Success Representative if you're unsure.

preferred_lang.description:
The preferred language of the contact.
This should be supplied in ISO 639-1 format.

prefix.description:
The contact's title.
Ometria accepts any of the following: Mr, Mrs, Miss, Ms.
If the gender field is left empty, Ometria infers gender from the prefix (e.g. Mr will be 'm', Ms will be 'f', etc.)
max length: 16.

store_ids.description:
An array of strings for which stores the customer belongs to.
max length: 31, lower case.
If left empty this field will be set to 'null'.

subscriptions.description: Marketing opt-in preferences for additional channels, e.g. direct mail. Each key is a channel name and its value describes the contact's preference for that channel.

allow_marketing.description: Whether the contact is opted in/out for direct mail marketing. If left out, this implies unspecified.

timestamp.description:
The date and time the contact updated their direct mail marketing preference. Only provide if known.
Follow ISO 8601 DateTime format with timezone offset YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+Z

value.description: The contact's postal address, supplied as a JSON-encoded string. Supported fields: "address_line_1", "city", "state", "postcode", "country_code" (2 characters, upper case, following ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and "address_type" (e.g. "shipping").

timestamp_acquired.description:
The date and time the contact was 'acquired'. Only provide this if known.
Follow ISO 8601 DateTime format with timezone offset YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+Z

timestamp_subscribed.description:
The date and time the contact was 'subscribed'. Only provide this if known.
Follow ISO 8601 DateTime format with timezone offset YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+Z

timestamp_unsubscribed.description:
The date and time the contact was 'unsubscribed'. Only provide if known.
Follow ISO 8601 DateTime format with timezone offset YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+Z

timezone.description: As defined in the tz database, max length: 64.

FieldForgetBulkResponse.description: The outcome of a bulk field forget submission: one result per submitted item, plus counts by outcome.

accepted.description: Number of items that created a new request.

duplicate.description: Number of items that matched a request already `pending` or `in_progress` and less than 24 hours old.

rejected.description: Number of items that failed validation and created no request.

request_id.description: Identifies this `POST /field-forget/bulk` call. If you sent an `X-Request-ID` header on the call, this is its value, so you can correlate it with your own logs; otherwise Ometria generates one.

results.description: One entry per submitted item, in the same order as submitted.

FieldForgetBulkResult.description: The outcome of one item from a bulk field forget submission.

id.description: The request ID. Use it with `GET /field-forget/{id}` to poll for the outcome. `null` for a `rejected` item, which created no request.

index.description: Position of this item in the submitted `requests` array.

message.description: Present only when `result` is `rejected`: what was wrong with this item.

profile_hash.description: Echoed only when the submitted value was actually a string.

result.description: `accepted`: a new request was created. `duplicate`: matched a request already `pending` or `in_progress` and less than 24 hours old; `id` is that existing request. `rejected`: the item failed validation and no request was created.

FieldForgetBulkSubmission.description: A batch of field forget request submissions.

requests.description: A non-empty list, capped at 100 items, of `profile_hash`/`fields` objects, each with the same shape `POST /field-forget` accepts.

FieldForgetErrorMessage.description: Error returned by the field forget endpoints.

example.message: fields must be a subset of email, phone
example.title: Bad Request

message.description: What was wrong with the request.

title.description: Short description of the error class.

FieldForgetPostResponse.description: Response to a field forget request submission

id.description: The request ID. Use it with `GET /field-forget/{id}` to poll for the outcome. An identical request that is still in flight and less than 24 hours old returns the ID of the existing request.

FieldForgetRequest.description: Describes a field forget request and its status

fields.description: The fields requested, sorted alphabetically and deduplicated.

items.description: A field that can be forgotten. This list is the set supported by the service and is kept in sync via the service's own spec test.

profile_hash.description: The profile hash of the profile the request was filed for (eg 27f4-f0b281-00003039).

api_request_id.description: Identifies the `POST /field-forget` call that filed this request. If you sent an `X-Request-ID` header on that call, this is its value, so you can correlate the request with your own logs; otherwise Ometria generates one. `null` for requests filed from the Ometria app.

origin.description: `api` for requests filed through this API, `app` for requests filed from the Ometria app.

status.description: Current state of the request. `pending`: accepted and queued. `in_progress`: being processed. info.description:
Welcome to the Ometria API reference.


The Ometria API is organized around the [REST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer) methodology, and it uses resource-oriented URLs, and common HTTP response codes to indicate API errors. All requests are authenticated using an API key which can be obtained from your account settings.

### HTTPS

All requests to the Ometria API MUST be carried out via HTTPS. API servers do not listen on unsecured HTTP ports to avoid the possibility of insecure information exchange.

### Message encoding

The V2 Ometria API uses JSON encoding for all data exchanges and assumes UTF-8 character encoding throughout.

### Rate limits

The Ometria API has a default rate limit of 4 requests per second per Ometria account. The /push/ endpoint allows 8 requests per second per Ometria account. If you expect to exceed this limit, please contact us.

In the case of your application being rate limited, the HTTP code 429 (too many requests) will be returned. In this case your application should reduce the number of requests it is trying to send.

post.description:
Erase a profile's `email` and/or `phone` while keeping the rest of the profile. For each requested field, Ometria clears the value on the profile. Nothing prevents the same value being added back to this profile later either.

`profile_hash` is the `id` of a profile, as returned by `GET /profiles/`.

Requests are processed asynchronously. A `202` means the request was accepted and queued; poll `GET /field-forget/{id}` until `status` is terminal. A request identical to one that is still `pending` or `in_progress` and less than 24 hours old returns the existing request's `id` (still `202`) rather than creating a new one, so retries are safe. Once a request has reached a terminal status, a new request for the same profile and fields is accepted again.

post.description:
Submit up to 100 field forget requests in a single call. Each item is judged and processed independently: a malformed item is rejected without blocking its siblings, and an item identical to a request still `pending` or `in_progress` and less than 24 hours old is reported as `duplicate` and returns that existing request's `id`, rather than creating a new one.

This always returns `202`, even when every item was rejected, so check each item's `result` field rather than the HTTP status. For each accepted or duplicate item, poll `GET /field-forget/{id}` with its `id` to find out how the request completed.

requestBody.description: `requests`: a non-empty list, capped at 100, of the same `profile_hash`/`fields` objects `POST /field-forget` accepts.

Preferences centre
